title: Sliding Through the Water...
text:
Sliding through the water,

I have come as far as the Island.

I have wandered among its breezes.

And along its coast I have run.


I came out of the sea full of seaweed,

my bathing suit clinging tight.

And after walking through the Island,

I slept beneath a tree.


What sumptuous solitude!

What splendid solitude!

And what a fatiguing life,

the life of the city!
editorial_note: The translation keeps the island as a bodily escape from the exhausting city.

title: The Wind...
text:
The wind

beats swords of ice.


-I will not open the window-


The wind

decapitates stars.


-I will not open the window-


The wind

carries tongues of fire.


-I will not open the window-


In telegrams of shadow

that the winds keep carrying,

the Great News can already be read,

the news that shakes the Universe...


-I will not open my window-
editorial_note: The translation keeps the repeated refusal to open the window against apocalyptic wind.

title: Wide Is the Sea; It Must Separate Us
text:
Wide is the sea; it must separate us;

our souls will remain entwined.

Like one last portrait, in our eyes

our gazes will shine impressed.


The ship I must take is in the harbor;

after this one, another will follow for you.

My arms will wait for you, I do not know where...

perhaps in some harbor... on a beach...!
editorial_note: The translation keeps the lovers separated by ships while their gazes remain imprinted.

title: They Were Green Like a Sea
text:
They were green like a sea,

with reflections of high sky.

-How well they knew how to look!-

those eyes I remember.


In the half-light they shone

with a mysterious light,

like two clear abysses

opened to a thousand desires.


For many hours I had near me

those green eyes,

looking at me imploringly,

and I tried not to see them!


And today, when I would like to look at them,

they are so far away... so far!
editorial_note: The translation keeps the remembered green eyes as sea, abyss, desire, and distance.

title: From What Badly Wounded Wheatfield?
text:
From what badly wounded wheatfield

did they go to lift you up,

my poor fallen angel?


Was it perhaps your destiny

to go so far away to end yourself,

and for that reason you were in such a hurry

when you departed?


Was the meeting in Castile,

and was that Castilian night

waiting for you at that hour

to receive you in its arms?


How unaware my life was

that your life was setting out

on a one-way journey

with no return and nothing more!...
editorial_note: The translation keeps the elegy as a series of questions around a final one-way journey.
